target_customer: AI and ML research teams and labs that run many experiments with coding agents
problem: Teams lose context between experiments and spend time on infrastructure, supervising agents and catching teammates up. Probe logs runs, metrics and decisions so agents build on past work.
business_model: Software platform for teams; pricing not stated
product_category: Experiment tracking and research workspace for AI agents

previous_startups: An EdTech startup backed by the Qatar Foundation
Chemistry Catalyst Fellowship (co-founded with Chemistry VC)

founders.background_notes: Speculative decoding research at Berkeley; LoRA fine tuned inference at Databricks and machine translation at Apple per YC page

founders.background_notes: Worked on YouTube Shorts and Android XR hand interaction at Google per YC page

competitors.name: Weights & Biases
competitors.what: Experiment tracking, model registry and sweeps, with Weave for LLM work
competitors.traction_then: Market standard for ML experiment tracking

competitors.name: Trackio
competitors.what: Free local first tracking library from Hugging Face

competitors.name: Neptune
competitors.what: Experiment tracking platform that announced sunsetting its developer platform on March 5, 2026 and was acquired by OpenAI per roundups

technical_complexity.rationale: Run logging, agent integrations with Claude Code, Codex and Cursor, and compute setup are standard engineering with some hard integration parts.

defensibility.rationale: Accumulated experiment history can create lock-in, but W&B and open source tools cover tracking and copying agent integrations is easy.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Incumbents add agent features (W&B Weave); no action against Probe reported.

market_need_then: Coding agents began running research experiments in 2026, and roundups note the tools to observe and debug agents have diverged from classic experiment tracking.

branding.domain_note: Uses useprobe.ai with docs on prbe.ai subdomains (company site); not probe.com
branding.community_and_virality: A Fondo blog post covered the launch on 2026-10-21

brand_strength.rationale: Many other companies called Probe, including a YC incident management startup, so the name is confusable; only one launch write-up found.

outcome_analysis: Probe is a Spring 2026 YC company still operating with no outcome yet. The three Berkeley founders have ML infrastructure experience, but the category has entrenched trackers and open source options, so Probe must win on agent native workflows and shared context to raise.
notes: No funding found. No acquisition or shutdown news found. Competitor list comes from 2026 roundup posts, not dated launch coverage. YC page shows no team size while another source says 3. One search result describes a different Probe (incident management, P26); excluded.
